storylines.label: Claude Fable
storylines.latest_title: Working with Claude Fable 5 in Claude Cowork | Claude by Anthropic

prior_narrative.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5 in late June as long-horizon models "made safe for general use." A same-day companion post revealed a US export-control suspension had already been lifted, with a fresh redeploy starting July 1 alongside new cyber-safeguard classifiers and a first-draft jailbreak severity framework.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Anthropic published a second enterprise case study — Base44 says it trusts Fable 5 with its hardest product and engineering work, echoing Cognition's July 10 report without resolving the reported Max-plan access narrowing.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Two independent enterprise case studies in five days is a stronger adoption signal than one — useful evidence for justifying long-horizon agentic coding trust with Fable 5, though the underlying access-path question stays open.

status.state: Enterprise trust deepening · Max-plan access still unresolved
status.detail: Fable 5 launched "made safe for general use" in late June with an export-control suspension already lifted; a July 5 hands-on report flagged Max access narrowing, and case studies since — a field guide, Cognition's eight-hour Devin run, then Base44's — show trust compounding without resolving the access question.

beats.headline: Same-day post reveals the export-control suspension already lifted, redeploy starts July 1
beats.summary: Anthropic's companion post confirms a US export-control suspension has been lifted, with the model returning July 1 alongside new cyber-safeguard classifiers and a first-draft jailbreak severity framework.

beats.headline: Hands-on Fable 5 ships real code — but Max-plan access reportedly narrows
beats.summary: A builder uses Fable 5 to push sqlite-utils toward a 4.0 stable release, noting his Claude Max subscription's access to the model is closing within days.

beats.headline: Anthropic publishes a builder field guide for Fable 5
beats.summary: A practitioner guide on finding unknowns before, during, and after implementation with Fable 5 — documentation, not a new status signal on the access question.

beats.headline: Cognition and Base44 both trust Fable 5 with their toughest engineering work
beats.summary: Two independent 'Working at the frontier' case studies in five days — Cognition's eight-hour unattended overnight Devin runs, then Base44's hardest product and engineering work — show enterprise trust compounding.

open_questions: Is the reported end of Fable 5 access on Claude Max subscriptions an official, product-wide change, and what happens after it?
Does the July 1 redeploy restore standard private-inference terms, or does a data-sharing requirement persist for any deployment path?
Is Fable 5 / Mythos 5 redeploying beyond Bedrock — first-party API or other clouds — on private-inference terms?
Do Cognition's and Base44's enterprise uses of Fable 5 run through access paths insulated from the reported Max-plan narrowing?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you're piloting long unattended agent runs, Cognition's eight-hour production-ready benchmark and Base44's complex-engineering use of Fable 5 are useful reference points — but confirm your own access path (API, Bedrock, or Max-plan) hasn't hit the reported narrowing before depending on it.

storylines.label: Sol Luna
storylines.latest_title: [AINews] OpenAI launches GPT 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Codex becomes ChatGPT superapp

prior_narrative.tldr: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 Sol on June 26 as its next flagship, pairing coding, science, and cybersecurity gains with its most advanced safety stack. A day later the family shipped only to a restricted trusted-partner tier, alongside an unrelated Anthropic release the same day.
prior_narrative.whats_new: GPT-5.6 — Luna, Terra, and Sol — reached general availability on July 9, with OpenAI's own launch post landing the same day as Simon Willison's independent GA writeup.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: The GA move ends the two-week restricted-partner window and adds a three-tier lineup (Luna/Terra/Sol) with per-tier pricing, so integrations built against the preview or partner tier should re-check access and re-evaluate cost/latency against the new tiers before defaulting to the largest model.

status.detail: Preview (Jun 26) -> restricted partner access (Jun 27) -> general availability (Jul 9).

beats.headline: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol with an upgraded safety stack
beats.summary: First look at the next-generation model, ahead of any public release.

beats.headline: Family ships to trusted partners only, not the general public
Luna, Terra, and Sol open to everyone with tiered per-token pricing
beats.summary: Luna prices at $1/$6 per 1M input/output tokens as the smallest of the three sizes.

open_questions: What are Terra's and Sol's exact per-token prices relative to Luna's $1/$6?
Does GA access carry the same safety commitments OpenAI described in the June 26 preview?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you were on the restricted GPT-5.6 tier, re-check your access and quota now that GA is open, and benchmark Luna's $1/$6-per-1M-token tier against your current model before defaulting to Sol for cost-sensitive agent loops.
